items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: And then Mel called one day and said, “Oh, Thad Jones and I are starting a band and we would like you to play in the band. Would you be interested?”

ctx.x: They’re nasty, oh my. Well you’ve been with some of the great big bands, from Gerald Wilson through Benny Carter. Tell me how the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band kind of gelled into a great organization.

Gee. I knew Thad, I had met him in San Francisco when he was with Count Basie, and we played together at an after hours place there. And I met Mel through playing with Peggy Lee in New York and then eventually with Benny Goodman. We went to Russia and Mel was the drummer with Benny Goodman. And I knew both of these guys separately. I didn’t know them together. And then Mel called one day and said, “Oh, Thad Jones and I are starting a band and we would like you to play in the band. Would you be interested?” I…
I wish I could have seen something at the Vanguard, just to see the band fit in there first of all. It must have been a little crowded.
